Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 64, verse 2:

﴿He is the One who created you, and among you is the disbeliever and among you is the believer﴾. In the interpretation of this verse there are two views. The first: He who created you, so it was obligatory upon each one of you to believe in Him, but among you some disbelieved and among you some believed. Thus, according to this view, disbelief and belief are from the acquisition (iktisab) of the servant. The second: the meaning is that He created you in two categories: among you He created one who is a believer and among you He created one who is a disbeliever. Thus, according to this view, belief and disbelief are what Allah has decreed upon each individual. The first is more apparent, because His connecting it to "created you" with the particle fa' (then/so) requires that disbelief and belief occur after the creation, not in the original creation itself.

Creation of the heavens and the earth in truth; its meaning has been mentioned in several places. ﴿And He shaped you and perfected your shapes﴾: a mention of the blessing of the beautiful form of the children of Adam, for they are the most beautiful in form of all kinds of animals, even though some people are found to be ugly in appearance. That does not remove them from the beauty of the human form; rather, he is ugly only when compared with one who is more beautiful than him among people. It has also been said: it means the intellect and the understanding with which the human being was singled out. The first is more preferred, because "ṣūrah" (form) is only applied to outward shape.

﴿Has there not come to you﴾ is addressed to the Quraysh and the rest of the disbelievers. ﴿They said, "Will mere humans guide us?"﴾ Its meaning is that they found it hard to accept that God would send a human being, or they were too proud to follow a human being. The word *bashar* (human being) applies to both the single person and the group. ﴿Those who disbelieve claim that they will never be resurrected.﴾ Ibn ʿUmar said: "*Zaʿama* (claimed) is a metaphor for lying."

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 64, verse 9:

﴿يَوْمَ يَجْمَعُكُمْ﴾ The factor (al-'amil) governing "yawma" (the day) is either "latub'athunna" (you will certainly be resurrected), or it is an omitted verb whose estimated form is "udhkur" (remember). It is also possible that it is a subject (mubtada'), with its predicate being ﴿ذَلِكَ يَوْمُ ٱلتَّغَابُنِ﴾ (that is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain), meaning the Day of Resurrection. "Al-taghabun" is used metaphorically from the mutual cheating of people in trade (taghabun al-nas fi al-tijara), and this occurs when the blessed (al-sa'ada') triumph with Paradise. It is as if they have cheated the wretched (al-ashqiya') regarding their abodes, the places they would have descended to had they been among the blessed. Thus "al-taghabun," on this reading, carries the meaning of "al-ghabn" (loss/cheating). It is not according to the common usage of the form "tafa'ala," which implies two parties, as in your saying "tadarraba" (they struck one another) and "taqatala" (they fought one another); rather, it is a single act, like your saying "tawadda'a" (he humbled himself). Ibn 'Atiyya and al-Zamakhshari said: it means the descent of the blessed into the abodes of the wretched and the descent of the wretched into the abodes of the blessed, and "al-taghabun," on this reading, is between two parties. He said: and in it is a mockery of the wretched, because their descent into Hell is not, in reality, a loss for the blessed.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 64, verse 11–18:

﴿No calamity befalls except by the permission of Allah﴾. It is possible that by "calamity" he means misfortunes, and he singled them out for mention because they are the most significant for people. Or he means all events, whether good or bad, and "by the permission of Allah" is an expression for His decree and His will, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever believes in Allah – He will guide his heart﴾. It was said: its meaning is, whoever believes that everything occurs by the permission of Allah, Allah will guide his heart to submission and contentment with the decree of Allah. This is the best (interpretation), but generality is better than it.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 64, verses 14–15:

﴿Indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them﴾. Its occasion of revelation: some people embraced Islam and wanted to emigrate, but their spouses and children discouraged them from emigrating, so Allah warned them against obeying them in that. It was also said: it was revealed concerning ʿAwf ibn Mālik al-Ashjaʿī. He wanted to go out for jihad, but his family and children gathered and complained about his leaving them, so he took pity on them and returned. Then he regretted it and resolved to punish them, so the verse was revealed warning against the trial of children. Then Allah, the Exalted, turned him away from punishing them with His words: ﴿And if you pardon and overlook and forgive﴾, the verse. Yet the wording of the verse remains general in its warning against whoever among one's family and children becomes an enemy to a person, whether their enmity is due to religion or to worldly matters. ﴿And Allah has with Him a great reward﴾: an encouragement toward the Hereafter and a discouragement from wealth and children, by which people have been tested.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on Surah 64, verse 16:

﴿So fear God as much as you are able﴾. It is said: this abrogates (naskh) His saying: ﴿Fear God with the fear due to Him﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 102]. It is narrated that when ﴿with the fear due to Him﴾ was revealed, it weighed heavily on the people until ﴿as much as you are able﴾ was revealed. It is also said that there is no abrogation between them, because "the fear due to Him" is within what you are able to do, since no one can do anything except what he is able to do. On this view, this verse clarifies that one. Through the qualification "as much as you are able" it guards against compulsion, forgetfulness, and whatever the servant is not held accountable for.

As for the i'rab (grammatical analysis) of ﴿as much as you are able﴾ (ma istaṭa'tum), the phrase "mā" is adverbial of time (ẓarfiyya). ﴿Good for yourselves﴾ (khayran li-anfusikum) is in the accusative by an implied verb that does not appear, according to Sibawayh. It is also said that it is the object of "anfiqū" (spend), since "khayr" here means wealth. It is also said that it is an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, its sense being: "spend in a good manner for yourselves."

﴿And whoever is protected from the greed of his own soul﴾: this was mentioned in Surah al-Hashr [59:9].
﴿If you lend to Allah a goodly loan﴾ is mentioned in al-Baqarah [2:245]. ﴿And Allah is Appreciative and Forbearing﴾ is mentioned in the section on language.
